title: The unique threshold bound state of the SU(N) BFSS model
main_claim: For every N>=2, the undeformed SU(N) BFSS Hamiltonian (form closure of the averaged squared supercharges on the gauge-invariant full space, centre of mass removed) has a one-dimensional L^2 kernel. That kernel is Spin(9)-invariant and fermion-even. The proof runs a simultaneous induction on N. A BMN-type massive index on gauge and G-torus invariants equals p(N). At large coupling the massive kernel is split into p(N)-1 proper-cluster profile lines plus a whole-block part valued in K_N. An exterior Hardy-type estimate rules out norm at intermediate scales, and a gap/recovery argument gives dim K_N = 1.

issues.description: The claim that the full-collapse profile's norm equals exactly the atom at zero is justified only by saying it follows 'by the same inner-ball and shrinking-physical-ball comparison' used for the proper strata. The argument looks right, because Lemma intermediate-scales at size N applies with bounded undeformed graph norm after a fixed cutoff. However, the order-of-limits bookkeeping is not written out for this case.
issues.evidence: "Lemma~\ref{lem:intermediate-scales}, now available at size N, identifies its norm with exactly the atom at zero by the same inner-ball and shrinking-physical-ball comparison"

issues.description: Three claims are argued tersely: that the fast section is untwisted under block permutations and Spin(3)xSpin(6), via a graph-vacuum argument on last-six configurations plus connectedness, and that the Berry form vanishes. The proper-profile counting in sec 7 (one line per partition) and the G-action on profiles depend on these claims. I found no error but did not verify them in full detail.
issues.evidence: "Agreement on last-six configurations proves agreement everywhere. The same construction gives covariance under Spin(3)xSpin(6)."

coverage: I read all seven sections in full: the algebra section (square formula, coercivity, domains, rotation anticommutator, singlet/parity), the massive index section (potential coercivity, common domain, BMN normal modes, stabilizer character, slice compactness, recovery), fast analysis, lifts, profiles and the exterior estimate, and the counting section. Checked numerically with explicit real 16x16 Spin(9) gammas: the spin identity (alg:spin-identity), the mass-spin identity C(v) = -3/4 T - 1/2 S(R(v)), skewness of R(v), the existence of the common two-plane, gamma^3 = sigma on it, and the formula R(u) = sigma(-2E12+E45+E67+E89). Checked by hand: the Spin(3)-averaging identity behind the 2/3 coercivity, and the boson/fermion zero-point cancellation for the BMN normal modes, which both equal 16l^2+16l+6. Also checked: the abelian centre oscillator, the Hardy constant (d_C-2)/2 >= 7/2 and the resulting 5/(2 sqrt2) > 1, the weighted IMS identity, the case split of the tightness scaling (m' vs sqrt h'), and the gap/pairing/recovery counting logic (p(N)-1+M <= p(N)). Not fully re-derived: every Sobolev/oscillator-moment bound in the fast-line perturbation, and the details of the chart-transition maps.
